sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Dougherty County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Two pieces of the same county department split the work: the Tax Department collects, and the Board of Assessors sets values. Dougherty County runs its Tax Department under an appointed tax director instead of an elected tax commissioner. That department receives property tax returns and collects ad valorem tax for the county, the City of Albany, the school board and the State of Georgia.

The bills it handles cover real estate, automobiles, personal property, mobile homes and timber. The Board of Assessors is part of the department and places a value on every real and personal property parcel. Owners can look up a parcel on qPublic, and the county news page links a video walkthrough of the search.

  • Value, notice of assessment or appeal: Board of Assessors, 229-431-2130 or DocoAssessor@dougherty.ga.us.
  • County millage rate: adopted by the Dougherty County Board of Commissioners.
  • School millage rate: set separately by the Dougherty County Board of Education.
  • Payment, bill dates and a payoff figure for a closing: the Tax Department.

sections.h2: What did the 2026 revaluation change for Dougherty County owners?
sections.html:
The 2026 notices followed the county's first comprehensive revaluation in more than 10 years, and many owners saw large changes in fair market value. A county news release dated August 31, 2026 stresses that a Notice of Assessment is not a tax bill. It lists the fair market value, homestead details and appeal instructions, and the real tax comes later, after appeals close and the digest and millage rates are final.

County commissioners told residents at that meeting that the assessors, not the commission, decide values. The commission adopts the county budget and the county rate, and it said a higher value does not automatically produce an equal rise in the county bill.

House Bill 581 adds a second layer. It generally caps yearly growth in the taxable value of qualifying homesteads for taxing authorities that take part, and each county, city and school district could choose to opt out. The Dougherty County Board of Education opted out after public hearings, and the school system says opting out leaves existing homestead exemptions in place. A May 2026 update from the Georgia Department of Revenue says SB 33, the HOME Act of 2026, removes the opt-out, applies the statewide floating exemption from January 1, 2027, and uses 2026 values as the baseline. Ask the Tax Department how that change reaches your school bill.

sections.h2: How does a Dougherty County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
You file a written appeal with the Board of Assessors within 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. For the 2026 notices the county gave a closing time of 11:59 p.m. on October 5, 2026, and that window has passed. Later notices carry their own mailing date, so count 45 days from the date printed on yours.

The Department of Revenue says an appeal may rest on taxability, value, uniformity or the denial of an exemption, and it goes on the state's uniform appeal form. On that form you pick the route you want. The chosen route decides who hears the case.

  • County Board of Equalization.
  • Hearing officer.
  • Arbitrator.

County leaders urged owners whose value doubled or tripled to use the process, and the assessors take questions at 229-431-2130. Bring a recent sale of a similar Albany house, repair estimates or photos of defects. A flood-prone lot near the Flint River or a roof near the end of its life are the kind of facts that support a lower value.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special assessments apply in Dougherty County?
sections.html:
Homeowners who owned and lived in the house on January 1 can claim the state homestead exemption, and the Revenue Department says the application is open through the 45-day appeal window, not only to April 1. The standard state exemption takes $2,000 off the 40 percent assessed value for county and school tax. Owners 65 and older can claim a $4,000 county exemption when household income does not exceed $10,000 for the prior year, with the retirement income carve-outs the state describes.

Land has its own programs. The Board of Assessors lists three, all filed between January 1 and April 1 with a $25 application fee:

  • Preferential agricultural assessment, which assesses qualifying farmland at 30 percent of fair market value in place of 40 percent.
  • Conservation use assessment, which values agricultural, timber, environmentally sensitive and residential transitional land at current use value.
  • The Georgia Forest Land Protection Act, which exempts land used in good faith to grow trees, timber and wood fiber.

The owner must be an individual or family farm corporation, estate, trust or non-profit, must keep the qualifying use for 10 years, and may hold no more than 2,000 acres statewide in conservation use programs. Ask the Tax Department about any extra local exemptions Dougherty County layers on top of the state ones.

sections.h2: What do the Dougherty County numbers look like?
sections.html:
Dougherty County is a shrinking, renter-heavy county in southwest Georgia built around the City of Albany. The county was carved from Baker County in 1853, covers 326 square miles of land by its own count, and is known for quail plantations, the Flint River and cypress swamps. Albany State University and Albany Technical College anchor higher education, and the Albany Civil Rights Institute and Flint RiverQuarium draw visitors.

sections.h2: What happens to the property tax bill when you sell a Dougherty County house?
sections.html:
Whoever owned the property on January 1 owes the tax for the whole year, and Georgia law gives no refund for a part year. A seller who closes in March still faces a bill that covers all twelve months, so the contract and the closing statement decide how the buyer and seller split it. The Department of Revenue says most counties send bills with 60 days to pay and a usual due date of December 20, but Dougherty County's own dates come from the Tax Department.

Before you list, gather three things:

  • The parcel number from qPublic and a copy of the 2026 notice.
  • A current balance from the Tax Department, including any older unpaid years.
  • Your homestead status, since the exemption follows whoever owned and lived in the house on January 1.

Houses in Albany with deferred repairs, tenants or probate questions often sell as-is for cash, and the tax balance is simply paid from proceeds. Tax liens are filed with the clerk, so confirm the balance and any lien on record before you sign.

faqs.q: Is a Dougherty County Notice of Assessment a tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The notice shows the property's fair market value, homestead information and appeal instructions. The actual tax is calculated later, after appeals close, the tax digest is final and the county, city and school millage rates are adopted.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Dougherty County assessment?
faqs.a: No. The county set October 5, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. as the last moment to appeal the 2026 notices, 45 days after mailing. Future notices will show their own mailing date, and the 45 days run from that date.

faqs.q: Who sets the millage rate in Dougherty County?
faqs.a: The Board of Commissioners sets the county rate, and the Board of Education sets the school rate. The Board of Assessors only determines value. Commissioners said the county rate is decided after the appeal period ends and the digest is complete.

faqs.q: Did the Dougherty County school system opt out of the HB 581 exemption?
faqs.a: Yes, the Board of Education opted out after public hearings and said existing homestead exemptions stay. A May 2026 Revenue Department update says SB 33 removes the opt-out, with the statewide floating exemption applying from January 1, 2027, so ask the Tax Department how it will apply to you.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax if I sell my Dougherty County house mid-year?
faqs.a: The owner on January 1 is responsible for the full year, and Georgia does not refund a partial year. In practice the closing statement allocates the bill between buyer and seller, so ask the Tax Department for the balance before closing.
